add: smp, a + b + c + ... + n_term; can be list.
mul: smp, a * b * c * ... * n_term; can be list.
sqrt: smp, value x when multiplied to itself gives a(input), thus; x*x = a; only 1 input
arithmetic_average: smp, average; (a+b+c+...+n_term)/(no of terms), can be list
abs: smp, absolute, if number n is < 0; then -(n), if 0; then 0; if > 0 then n.; 1 input only
min: smp, minimum of the given values, can be list
max: smp, maximum of the given values, can be list
random-int: cmplx, generated a random integer between given inputs. 2 inputs(min, max);
random: cmplx, generated a random number using computer entropy. generates a 13-16 digit number, HIGH RESOURCE!, NO inputs
round: smp, rounds number to given decimal places, 2 inputs(input_number, decimal_places)
clamp: adv, makes the value stay under desired values, 3 inputs(input_value, min_value, max_value)
normalize: adv, returns normalized value restricted to 0 - 1. 5 inputs(input_value, min_value, max_value, new_min, new_max)
1D_lerp: adv, Linear interpolation, 3 inputs(value{0-1}, a-point, b-point
distance: smp, gives distance between 2 points on a 1-D axis, value is absolute, 2 inputs(start-point, end-point)
receprocal: smp, receprocal of x returns 1/x. 1 input(value)
sign: adv, sign(x) returns -1 if x<0; returns 0 if x=0; returns 1 if x<1. 1 input(value)
abs_equal: adv, absolute_equal gives Voolean True/False for 2 values if they are close enough by a certain threshold(value), 3 inputs(a_value, b_vlaue, threshold). NOTE-FLOATING POINT ERROR exists
apx_eql: adv, approx_equal gives Boolean True/False for 2 values if they are 'close enough' or not by a threshold(relative), 3 inputs(a_value, b_value, threshold)
percent_equal: adv, percent_equal gives Boolean True/False for 2 values if they are 'close enough' or not by a threshold in percent, 3 inputs(a_value, b_value, threshold)
in_range: adv, in_range tell if value(x) is between low_value, and high_value, such that; low<x<high; if yes, then TRUE, else FALSE. 3 inputs(value, low_value, high_value).
wrap: adv, value x to a specific range [min, max] by wrapping it back to the start if it exceeds the maximum, or back to the end if it falls below the minimum, 3 inputs(value, min, max)
